key_insight: EATS improves medical reasoning agents’ tool selection by retrieving relevant past tool-use experiences rather than relying only on tool descriptions.
clinical_relevance: Experience-guided tool selection could support medical image question answering and report generation, though clinical benefit is not established.
method: Store prior queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback.
Retrieve relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries.
Expand memory with test-time experience without ground-truth supervision.
evidence_signal: Across four public datasets and three multimodal LLMs, the abstract reports consistent gains in tool selection and downstream task performance, without numerical effect sizes.
watch_item: Self-evaluated memories may retain errors; reliability under clinical distribution shifts requires further validation.
paper_title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
